title: Copilot Studio: enforce safe sharing by detecting credential oversharing

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: Microsoft's feature-settings reference says credential-sharing restrictions are on by default, contrary to the briefing's off/detect-only default. The no-licence and no-credit-impact assurances lack supporting documentation, and several control paths and the proposed CLI equivalent need correction or qualification.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Copilot Studio evaluates agent connections at share or publish time and can prevent unsafe credential sharing.
claims.quote: When you enforce this setting, Copilot Studio evaluates the connections used by an agent and can prevent the agent from being shared or published when a connection violates the organization's connection-sharing policy.

claims.claim: An unsafe agent must use at least one connection that does not allow credential sharing.
claims.quote:
An agent is considered unsafe for sharing when both of the following conditions are true:
- The agent uses at least one connection that doesn’t allow credential sharing.

claims.claim: The unsafe connection must also use design-time credentials instead of asking each user to authenticate.
claims.quote: The connection uses credentials supplied at design time instead of asking each user to authenticate with their own credentials.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: All sharing allowed detects and informs without blocking, whereas Safe sharing enforced blocks applicable unsafe share or publish paths.
claims.quote:
| All sharing allowed | Copilot Studio detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use, but doesn’t block sharing. |
| Safe sharing enforced | Copilot Studio blocks applicable publish or share paths when an agent is unsafe for sharing. |

claims.claim: Makers see connection-sharing warnings or errors in Agent status.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio surfaces connection-sharing violations in **Agent status**. For an authenticated agent that you didn't share, a warning appears indicating how many connections violate the administrator's connection-sharing policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Affected tools are marked Blocked with a Sharing policy violation message.
claims.quote: These tools are marked as **Blocked** with a **Sharing policy violation** message explaining that a connection violates the administrator's connection-sharing policy.

claims.claim: Enforcement prevents sharing a violating agent with viewers or end users.
claims.quote: You can't share an agent that violates a connection-sharing security policy with a user who has viewer or end-user access.

claims.claim: Enforcement prevents sharing a violating agent with everyone in the organisation for end-user access.
claims.quote: Similarly, you can't share the agent with everyone in your organization for end-user access.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Publish becomes unavailable when publishing an already-shared agent would expose an unsafe connection.
claims.quote: For authenticated agents, an agent that you didn't share can publish successfully, while an agent you already shared with another user is blocked from publishing when enforcement applies.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: For channels without a separate Share action, enforcement occurs primarily at publishing.
claims.quote: Some channels make an agent available as part of publishing and don’t provide a separate **Share** action. In these scenarios, enforcement occurs primarily when the maker publishes the agent.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: As dependency enforcement expands, an unsafe called flow or agent can make its parent unsafe for sharing.
claims.quote: As dependency-based enforcement becomes available, an unsafe dependency can cause the calling agent to be treated as unsafe for sharing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enforcement does not retroactively unshare or disable existing agents.
claims.quote: Enabling enforcement doesn’t retroactively unshare or disable agents that were previously shared.

claims.claim: The sharing control does not block agents while they are running.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn’t block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.claim: The safe-sharing setting is an environment-level control for Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: The **Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials** setting is an environment-level control for Microsoft Copilot Studio agents.

claims.claim: Administrators can configure safe sharing for an environment group through Security > Threat detection.
claims.quote: You can configure the setting for an individual environment or an environment group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Approved service principals, API keys or managed identities can permit publishing when the associated connection supports the scenario.
claims.quote: Agents that use an approved system identity, such as a service principal, API key, or managed identity, can be published when the associated connection supports the scenario.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The companion credential-choice control immediately changes all tools for all agents in the affected environment to require end-user credentials.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A shared agent using maker credentials can let recipients act with the maker's permissions in connected services.
claims.quote: When an agent uses such a connection, other users of the agent can perform operations by using the permissions associated with the maker's credentials.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Detection findings can identify affected agents, connectors and related flows for remediation.
claims.quote: Use warnings and recommendations in Copilot Studio and administrative experiences to identify agents that use unsafe connections. The information can include the affected connector, the credential type, and whether the risk comes from a related agent or flow.

claims.claim: Configuring safe sharing requires permission to manage settings for the target environment.
claims.quote: To configure **Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials**, you need permission to manage settings for the target Power Platform environment.

claims.where: Scope: Roles; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Environment Admin is the role needed to change the safe-sharing mode for a single environment, without qualification.
claims.quote: If the environment has a Dataverse database, a user must be assigned the System Administrator role instead of the Environment Admin role to have full admin privileges.
claims.fix: Remove the unqualified '(Environment Admin)' and the assertion that Environment Admins can relax this setting. Retain the feature page's requirement for permission to manage environment settings; if naming roles, explain the Dataverse distinction at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security#predefined-security-roles and the feature-settings reference's System Administrator or equivalent requirement.

claims.claim: Environment-group administration requires a tenant administrator with appropriate group access.
claims.quote: Any subsequent changes can only be made by a tenant administrator with appropriate edit rights at the environment group level.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/environment-groups for the tenant-administrator and group-edit-rights requirement.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Safe sharing can be published as an environment-group rule that locks local settings and is inherited by new member environments.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform embedded maker credentials sharing environment group PowerShell REST API automation. Opened environment-groups, environment-groups-rules and the feature's security page; group configuration is documented, but publishing this setting as a rule is not.
claims.fix: Replace 'Publish the setting as an environment-group rule so new environments inherit it' with 'Configure the setting for the required environment group through Security > Threat detection.' Remove the claim that a published safe-sharing rule locks individual environments; the feature-specific page documents group configuration but not that rule lifecycle.

claims.claim: In the shared autonomous-agent model, a workflow used as a tool accepts only end-user credentials.
claims.quote: If your agent calls a workflow as a tool, that workflow can only accept end user credentials for authentication. Workflows that use any maker-only credentials aren't supported for autonomous agents.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent#share-an-autonomous-agent-for-users-to-run-preview and explicitly qualify this as the shared autonomous-agent preview, not a general limitation on all autonomous agents.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The safe-sharing setting is included and requires no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio embedded maker credentials sharing safe sharing enforced licensing license billing credits default. Opened both feature pages and managed-environment-licensing; read billing-licensing search excerpt. No passage states that this setting needs no licence.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'unknown'. Replace 'No licence for the setting' with 'The feature page lists permission to manage environment settings as a prerequisite but does not state a feature-specific licensing requirement.' Keep Managed Environments requirements separate and cite their licensing page.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Environment-group configuration requires Managed Environments.
claims.quote: Environment groups can only contain managed environments.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/environment-groups and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-licensing. State that Managed Environments require qualifying standalone licences or pay-as-you-go coverage for active usage; do not imply that grouping is universally licence-free.

claims.claim: The change has no Copilot Credit impact.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials" PowerShell API default licensing Copilot Credits; Copilot Studio embedded maker credentials sharing safe sharing enforced licensing license billing credits default. Feature pages and billing excerpts give no credit exemption for this control.
claims.fix: Replace 'No Copilot Credit impact' with 'Microsoft has not published a feature-specific Copilot Credit charge or exemption for this setting as of November 2026.' Do not extend that absence to the billing of agents or remediation testing.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cost rating 'none' is justified by the setting being included.
claims.quote: Page: 'cost: "none"' and 'None. Environment setting; Managed Environments for group scale.' Standard: 'none: included in licences already held, and the record or a Microsoft page says so.' The cited feature prerequisites establish permissions, not licence inclusion.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'low' for the known indirect work and replace the rationale with 'Low. Admin review and maker remediation take time; feature-specific licensing is not yet published, and environment groups require qualifying Managed Environments coverage.' Do not describe the change as licence-free.

claims.claim: The control is off by default and its default mode is detect-only.
claims.quote:
| Setting | Description | Default value |
| Don't let makers share agents with their own credentials embedded (recommended) | When **On**, makers can't share agents that include their own credentials. | On |

Replace the detect-only-default rationale with a statement that the reference lists blocking enabled by default, while the separate configuration article describes detection and enforcement modes without stating their default. Preserve the existing-agent enforcement gap.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls: fourth table row and following prose
claims.claim: pac admin set-governance-config --environment <environment-id> --protection-level Standard --limit-sharing-mode <mode> configures agent sharing limits.
claims.quote: Searched: pac admin set-governance-config limit-sharing-mode agents bot-limitSharingMode. Read the full set-governance-config parameters and Limit sharing's agent scripts; the CLI lists a generic sharing mode but no agent mapping, while agent scripts use bot-prefixed settings.
claims.fix: Replace the purported agent CLI equivalent with the documented PowerShell approach at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-sharing-limits#use-powershell-to-set-sharing-limits. Use Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <environment-id> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration <governance-configuration>, and specify that the object must preserve existing settings and update bot-limitSharingMode, bot-maxLimitUserSharing or bot-authoringSharingDisabled as appropriate. Do not equate the generic CLI flag with agent sharing settings.

claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration is a documented cmdlet usable to set agent sharing limits.
claims.quote:
Here's a PowerShell script that prevents agents from being shared with security groups and limits the number of viewers that can access an agent to 20.
Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration
